questions.question: What is the FIRST thing you should do before trying to register to vote?
options: A) Find your polling station
B) Check your eligibility
C) Research candidates
D) Get a voter ID card
questions.explanation: Checking eligibility (age, citizenship, residency) comes before registration. There is no point registering if you do not legally qualify.

questions.question: Why is meeting the voter registration deadline critical?
options: A) You get a fine if you miss it
B) Registration is just a formality — you can vote either way
C) Missing the deadline usually means you cannot vote in that election
D) It only affects postal voting
questions.explanation: In most jurisdictions, you must be registered before a specific deadline. Missing it typically means you cannot vote in that election cycle, even if you are fully eligible.

questions.question: You arrive at your assigned polling station and the queue is long. Polls close in 5 minutes. What should you do?
options: A) Leave — you missed your chance
B) Stay in the queue — if you are in line before closing time, you have the right to vote
C) Try another polling station nearby
D) Come back tomorrow
questions.explanation: In most democracies, if you are in the queue before the official closing time, you retain the right to vote. Do not leave the queue.

questions.question: What makes the secret ballot so important to democracy?
options: A) It speeds up the counting process
B) It allows people to vote without fear of punishment or coercion
C) It makes recounts easier
D) It prevents too many people from voting
questions.explanation: The secret ballot means no one can trace your vote back to you. This freedom from coercion or retaliation is fundamental to a genuine democratic choice.

questions.question: What is the difference between a media projection and an official election result?
options: A) There is no difference — they are legally the same
B) Media projections are based on exit polls and partial counts; official results are certified by electoral authorities
C) Official results are always announced first
D) Media projections are more accurate
questions.explanation: Media projections are estimates based on exit polls and early counts. Official results are certified by the returning officer or electoral authority and are legally binding. The two can differ.

questions.question: What is the correct channel for disputing an election result?
options: A) Social media campaigns
B) Approaching the winning candidate directly
C) Filing an official election petition through the courts within the legal deadline
D) Organising a re-vote independently
questions.explanation: Election disputes must go through official legal channels — typically an election petition filed in court within a strict deadline (usually 21–45 days). Unofficial methods have no legal standing.

questions.question: In India, what body is responsible for managing voter registration and conducting elections?
options: A) The Parliament of India
B) The Supreme Court of India
C) The Election Commission of India (ECI)
D) State Governments
questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is the independent constitutional authority responsible for administering elections and maintaining the electoral roll.

questions.question: What does 'indelible ink' on the finger signify in Indian elections?
options: A) The voter has been identified as a suspect
B) The voter has already cast their vote and cannot vote again
C) The voter's ballot was spoiled
D) The voter is a first-time voter
questions.explanation: Indelible (non-washable) ink is applied to a voter's finger after they vote. It is a simple, effective anti-fraud measure that prevents a person from voting more than once.

questions.question: After an election, what is the most important ongoing civic action you can take?
options: A) Wait for the next election in a few years
B) Celebrate or mourn the result and move on
C) Hold your elected representative accountable and stay engaged with democracy
D) Re-register for the next election immediately
questions.explanation: Democracy requires continuous engagement. Tracking your representative's actions, attending local meetings, and contacting officials between elections is how citizens hold power accountable.

questions.question: In the UK, what type of photo ID was made mandatory for voting in Great Britain since 2023?
options: A) Only a passport
B) Only a driving licence
C) Various forms of approved photo ID, including a free Voter Authority Certificate
D) A National Identity Card
questions.explanation: The UK now requires photo ID to vote. Accepted forms include a passport, driving licence, and others. Crucially, if you lack qualifying ID, you can apply for a free Voter Authority Certificate from your local council.
